first_impression.reaction: My assistant flagged it, so I read the first screen. The opening doesn't talk down to me about money, which I noticed and liked. But it's a consumer explainer on a stone I'd be choosing with our own jeweller. I let my assistant skim the rest for anything on the wedding side. There isn't much, and that's fine for this kind of page.

journey.quote: If you can comfortably choose either stone, the question is not whether you can afford natural.
journey.reaction: Good. Nobody's assuming I'm counting pennies. It's about what I want, not what I can stretch to.
Short and calm. I'd trust that more than a jeweller's blog.

journey.section: FTC naming rules / Australian Consumer Law
journey.quote: In 2019, FTC staff sent warning letters to eight companies.
journey.reaction: Too much regulation for me. US warning letters and ACCC rules are my jeweller's problem, not mine. My assistant would skip straight past this.

journey.quote: For a proposal abroad, carry the report and receipt.
journey.reaction: Fine for most people. For a significant stone travelling abroad I'd be thinking about security and insurance, not a receipt in a handbag. It reminds me this page isn't written with my situation in mind.

journey.section: Heirloom, rarity and what "forever" means to you
journey.quote: If the ring may be handed down, talk about it with whoever will one day wear it, and choose the story you would be happy to tell.
journey.reaction: This is the part that actually matters in my family. Handled gently, no lecture. I liked it.

journey.section: Worth it if, think twice if
journey.quote: You want the look and the size you love, and would rather put the difference towards the proposal, the honeymoon or the wedding itself.
journey.reaction: Saving-the-difference framing. Reasonable for most readers, but it isn't how we think, and it nudges the tone towards budget.

journey.section: From the ring to the destination
journey.quote: When you are ready, your Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments as your one point of contact, and the fee is agreed in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: One point of contact is right. But nothing here tells me they've handled three hundred guests or kept a wedding out of the press. On a diamond article I wouldn't expect it to, though.

unanswered_questions: Has this team delivered weddings at 200 to 400 guests with VIP logistics?
How do they handle discretion: NDAs, no social posting, press control?
Can they arrange secure transport and insurance for valuable jewellery travelling to a proposal or wedding abroad?
Is there a private-client or referral route rather than a general enquiry link?

turn_offs_found.quote: You want the look and the size you love, and would rather put the difference towards the proposal, the honeymoon or the wedding itself.
turn_offs_found.why: Edges towards value talk. Mild, but it's the line that made the page feel less like it was for me.

cta_reaction.quote: You can talk to a Wedded Concierge about a proposal or wedding abroad.
cta_reaction.why: I don't enquire through a public link on an explainer page. If someone I trust recommended them, I'd have my assistant reach out privately. This page doesn't hurt them, it just doesn't get them there.

top_3_changes: Soften the 'put the difference towards' bullet so the worth-it case is about preference, not saving money (e.g. lead with the look you love and leave the reallocation as a secondary thought).
Next to 'For a proposal abroad, carry the report and receipt', add one understated line about insuring and securely transporting a significant stone, only if the brand can back it up.
Offer a quieter private-client or referral route beside the general concierge link.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
No invented brand facts; capability gaps listed as unanswered questions
Ignored [[VERIFY]] markers, HTML comments and image slot notes
Did not invent problems; deferred business details (fee model, named Advisor, real weddings) not treated as must-fix

assumptions: Persona is provisional and uncalibrated. This is a top-of-funnel ring explainer not aimed at UHNW, so low relevance and enquiry scores reflect topic fit, not quality, and should carry limited weight.
